problem: Asynchronous control methods for cloud VLAs (RTC, A2C2) focus on temporal smoothing or residual correction, which suits fixed-base manipulators. On mobile robots under continuous displacement and irregular network latency, stale waypoints in past ego frames become spatially wrong and cause collisions.
motivation: Large VLAs must run in the cloud, so cloud-to-edge latency and jitter create a spatiotemporal mismatch between 'thinking' and 'control'. Black-box time prediction or delay-injection training is fragile under long-tail latency. The observation is that latency can be handled as geometry: delayed intent can be re-projected exactly with odometry history.
key_idea: Convert latency into a deterministic SE(2) spatial offset via a pose buffer to restore the VLA's intent, then use a PPO-Lagrangian CMDP RL adapter on a universal local sub-goal interface to trade off intent tracking against LiDAR safety.
insight: Explicit geometric realignment matters more than learned implicit compensation. Removing temporal alignment drops non-ideal SR from 76.7 to 36.7. The safety constraint is essential: without it, RER rises to 4.7 and SR falls to 23.3. Replacing the RL adapter with DWA lowers SR to 53.3 and raises CTE above 1.4. RTC has the lowest ideal-condition CTE but poor SR, so smooth tracking of stale intent is not safe.
method: Temporal pose buffer: a circular buffer of odometry at edge frequency; the pose at the VLA anchor timestamp is retrieved by linear interpolation for translation and shortest-path interpolation for heading.

Geometric re-projection: waypoints from the anchor ego frame are mapped to the current ego frame by p_E = T(t)^-1 T(t_a) p_A. Each new packet resets the anchor, so odometry drift stays within one communication cycle.

Standardized interface: the cloud VLA output is resampled to 5 waypoints at 20 cm spacing. The state is 10-D look-ahead points plus 144-D 2D LiDAR, and the action is a universal local sub-goal (dx, dy) in the ego frame, converted to velocity by a low-level controller.

CMDP with PPO-Lagrangian: the reward combines flow-tangent alignment, tanh cross-track error and smoothness. A separate safety cost combines an indicator and a linear penalty on LiDAR min-distance below R_safe. The dual variable lambda balances the two. Training uses OmniSafe.

Domain randomization: 10x10 m maps with 6 static and 6 dynamic obstacles, latency 0.3-1.5 s, packet loss up to 0.2, and blackouts. Actuator first-order lag, acceleration limits, noise and bias are randomized per episode.
Collision Radius Inflation: subtract a compensation value from raw LiDAR distances so a single policy adapts zero-shot to embodiments with larger footprints.

setting.backbone: Small PPO-Lagrangian RL policy (edge adapter, trained from scratch); cloud VLAs (SocialNav, TrackVLA, Nav-R2) are frozen
setting.training_data: Trained only in a randomized OmniSafe simulation (10x10 m maps, dynamic obstacles, latency and actuator randomization); no VLA fine-tuning
setting.observation: 2D LiDAR (144 beams) + odometry + delayed VLA local waypoints
setting.action_space: Universal local sub-goal (dx, dy) in the ego frame, converted to velocity commands
setting.simulator: OmniSafe (custom 3D navigation environment; Doggo and Racecar agents)

numbers.eval_set_note: 600 randomized episodes, Ideal (fast update, ~200 ms delay)
numbers.extra: simulated VLA waypoints at ~3 Hz; TTG on shared-success set (120/600)

numbers.eval_set_note: 600 randomized episodes, Non-ideal mixed degradation (heavy-tail latency, 15% loss, blackouts)
20 real trials over 4 scenarios (5 each); baseline is Direct VLA at 6/20 (30%)
numbers.extra: Unitree Go2, Wi-Fi ~200 ms RTT, 500-1500 ms injected jitter in one scenario

numbers_note: Sim benchmark is a custom OmniSafe setup, not a standard benchmark. Cross-embodiment sim results (Doggo/Racecar, SR 76-79) are omitted here as variants.
results: In simulation, AsyncShield reaches SR 80.0 (ideal) and 76.7 (mixed degradation) with RER 1.2/1.3. The strongest baseline, A2C2, gets 56.7/43.3, RTC 40.0/30.0 and Naive 20.0/16.7. On a real Unitree Go2 with three cloud VLAs, SR rises from 25-40% to 80-90% without any VLA fine-tuning.
limitations: Evaluated mainly in a custom 2D-LiDAR simulator with only 20 real trials per VLA, and no standard navigation benchmarks.
Relies on accurate odometry and 2D LiDAR only, with no semantic or 3D perception, so it targets planar environments.
Baselines RTC and A2C2 are re-adapted by the authors to waypoint navigation, which may not be a faithful comparison.
